pages.title: Flight Club Guidelines
pages.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.1 · Intro to P.E.
Flight Club

Flight Club Guidelines 🦉

Welcome to the Flight Club — the place where you take what you've learned and put it to the test. Every other week, a new movement challenge drops. You complete it, record it (or describe it), and earn Flight Club points. Here's how it works.

1
Mission
What Flight Club Is

Flight Club is the active part of Mission: Move!. Each module ends with a Flight Club challenge — a short, focused movement task connected to that module's topic. It's where the lesson meets the doing.

Some challenges train strength. Some train endurance. Some train coordination or sportsmanship. They're designed to take 5–15 minutes and require minimal equipment.

2
Rules
Flight Club Rules
  1. Read the full challenge first. Know what you're doing before you start.
  2. Warm up. 2–3 minutes of light cardio + dynamic stretches.
  3. Follow the steps in order. Don't skip — the order matters.
  4. Modify, don't quit. If a move is too hard, reduce reps or scale it down. If it's too easy, add reps.
  5. Cool down. 2–3 minutes of slow movement + static stretches.
  6. Hydrate — water before, during, after.
  7. Submit your proof. A photo, video, or written reflection — whatever the challenge asks for.
3
Crew
What Is the Flight Crew Check-In?

At the end of every challenge, you'll find a Flight Crew Check-In — two short reflection questions. Don't skip them. Real athletes train their thinking as much as their bodies. The Check-In asks you to notice what you did, why it worked (or didn't), and what you'd do differently next time.

Strong reflections earn extra Flight Club credit.

4
Safety
Safety First, Always
  • Check your space — clear of clutter, enough room to move
  • Wear safe shoes (closed-toe with grip)
  • Stop if something hurts beyond normal effort
  • Tell a trusted adult if you're unsure about a move
💡Did You Know?

Pro athletes call recovery and self-review "the secret 1%". They spend 80% of their time training, 19% in competition — and that final 1% reflecting on what worked. It's the smallest slice, but it's what separates good athletes from great ones. The Flight Crew Check-In is your 1%.

→What's Next

Ready? Your first Flight Club starts in Module 1.1, Week 2. Bring your A-game.

assignments.title: Week 1: VR Assignment - Fitness Park
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.1 · Intro to P.E.
Week 1

Welcome to your first project. You're going to design a virtual Fitness Park — a VR space that motivates someone (yourself or a future visitor) to actually move. Think like an athletic trainer: every zone has a purpose.

1
Step 1
Pick Your Landscape

Log in to your VR headset and choose any virtual landscape — beach, forest, mountain, park, anywhere. The setting should make movement feel inviting.

2
Step 2
Design 4 Activity Zones

Use IFX characters, signs, or models to design at least four activity zones. Each zone should clearly show or encourage a different type of physical movement. Use labels — signs, banners, or arrows — so a visitor knows what each zone is for.

3
Step 3
Required Zones & Examples
Zone Description IFX Idea
Jump ZoneHeart-pumping jumping movementJumping jacks IFX, jump pads
Dance ZoneRhythm and free movementDJ stand, speakers, dance IFX
Balance ZoneBalance and core focusBalance beams, yoga IFX, plank animations
Stretch ZoneCool-down and flexibilityToe touch, butterfly, seated yoga IFX
🏃Activity Cue

Extra Challenge (Optional):

  • Add a welcome sign at the entrance.
  • Include motivational messages ("Train your cardio!" or "Level Up Today").
  • Create a Fitness Trail path that guides visitors from zone to zone.
✅Check for Understanding

What you'll turn in: One clear screenshot of your complete Fitness Park with visible zones and activity examples.

📝Weekly Reflection

Why did you put the zones in the order you chose? Did you build a logical warm-up → workout → cool-down flow, or did you order them by something else? How do you know your design helps visitors actually move more — what specific element nudges them into action?

assignments.title: Week 2: Flight Club
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.1 · Intro to P.E.
Week 2
🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Kick off your athlete-in-training journey with three classic mobility moves. These open up your shoulders, back, and neck — the muscle groups you'll use in nearly every Flight Club to come.

1
Reach for the Sky Stretch

How to Do It:

  • Stand up tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
  • Stretch both arms up as high as possible, reaching for the sky.
  • Hold for 10 seconds, then relax.
  • Optional: Wiggle your fingers like you're grabbing stars!

Benefits: Stretches arms, shoulders, and back.

2
Hug Yourself Stretch

How to Do It:

  • Wrap your arms around yourself like you're giving a big hug.
  • Gently pull your shoulders forward while keeping your back straight.
  • Hold for 10 seconds, then switch arm positions (whichever arm was on top, switch it).

Benefits: Stretches shoulders and upper back.

3
Shoulder Rolls

How to Do It:

  • Stand or sit up straight.
  • Slowly roll your shoulders forward in a circular motion 5 times.
  • Then roll your shoulders backward 5 times.

Benefits: Loosens up the shoulders and neck.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video demonstrating the challenges. The more you do, the more points you get in Flight Club!

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which muscle group felt tightest during these stretches? Why might that area be tight — sports you play, sitting position, or something else?
  • Which stretch did you feel most in your body? How do you know it was working — what did you notice?

assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.2 · Warm-Ups & Cool-Downs
Week 4
🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Time to build that range of motion. Three static stretches that target your hamstrings, hips, and quads — the muscle groups athletes lock in the most.

1
Toe Touch Stretch (Waterfall Stretch)

How to Do It:

  • Stand up tall with feet together.
  • Slowly bend forward and reach for your toes, keeping legs straight.
  • Let your arms "flow down" like a waterfall.
  • Hold for 10 seconds, then slowly stand up.

Benefits: Stretches hamstrings (back of the thighs) and lower back.

2
Butterfly Stretch

How to Do It:

  • Sit on the floor with feet together and knees bent outward.
  • Hold your feet with your hands and gently push your knees toward the floor.
  • Keep your back straight and hold the stretch.
  • Optional: Pretend your legs are butterfly wings and gently flap them!

Benefits: Stretches the inner thighs and hips.

3
Flamingo Stretch (Quadriceps Stretch)

How to Do It:

  • Stand tall and bend one knee, bringing your foot behind you.
  • Hold your ankle with your hand and keep your balance.
  • Keep your knees close together and hold for 10 seconds.
  • Switch legs and repeat.
  • Optional: Extend one arm forward like a flamingo's neck!

Benefits: Stretches the front of the thigh (quadriceps) and improves balance.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video demonstrating the challenges. The more you do, the more points you get in Flight Club!

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which muscle group is tightest for you — hamstrings, hips, or quads? What evidence tells you (which stretch was hardest to hold, where you felt the most pull)?
  • Was this dynamic or static stretching? When in a workout would these stretches work best — before or after activity? Why?

5th Grade PE · Unit 1.3 · Muscular Strength & Endurance
Week 6
🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Real strength training. Three moves that build the muscle groups you use to push, pull, sprint, and stand tall.

1
Side Lunge Stretch (Skater Stretch)

How to Do It:

  • Stand with feet wide apart.
  • Bend one knee and shift your weight to that side, keeping the other leg straight.
  • Hold for 10 seconds, then switch sides.
  • Optional: Pretend you're an ice skater gliding side to side!

Benefits: Stretches inner thighs and hips.

2
Forearm Plank

How to Do It:

  • Get into a plank position with arms straight and back flat.
  • Hold for 30 seconds without dropping your belly.
  • Challenge: Try tapping one shoulder at a time while holding the plank.

Modification: Try a knee plank if needed.

Benefits: Builds core and upper body strength.

3
Push-Ups

How to Do It:

  • Start by lying on your stomach with your hands flat on the floor next to your shoulders.
  • Push your body up so your arms are straight and only your hands and toes are touching the ground.
  • Keep your body in a straight line — don't let your back sag or your hips rise.
  • Bend your elbows and lower your body until your chest is close to the floor, then push back up.
  • Try 5 push-ups to start.

Benefits: Builds upper body strength.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video demonstrating the challenges. The more you do, the more points you get in Flight Club!

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which fitness component were you training the most — strength or endurance? How do you know? (Hint: think about reps vs. resistance.)
  • Which muscle groups did the plank target? Name at least two, and explain how you felt them working.

assignments.title: Week 8: Flight Club
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.4 · Cardiovascular Fitness
Week 8
🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Time to train your cardiovascular system. Three high-energy challenges that get your heart rate into the target zone and keep it there.

1
Dance Party Freeze

How to Play:

  • Play upbeat music and dance non-stop.
  • When the music stops, you must freeze in place.
  • Repeat for 5-7 minutes.
  • Add challenges like "jump in place," "spin around," or "move like a robot."

Benefits: Increases heart rate, stamina, and coordination.

Party Freeze Dance Song — THE KIBOOMERS (suggested music)

2
Running Obstacle Course

How to Play:

  • Set up an obstacle course using cones, jump ropes, pillows, or other objects.
  • Include challenges such as:
    • Zigzag running around cones.
    • Jumping over small hurdles (pillows or markers).
    • Crawling under a rope (or imaginary tunnel).
    • Skipping to the finish line.
  • Time yourself and try again to improve.

Benefits: Improves endurance, agility, and coordination.

3
Jump Rope Challenge

How to Play:

  • Get a jump rope or pretend you're holding one.
  • Start with basic jumps for 30 seconds.
  • Challenge yourself with different variations:
    • Fast jumping (see how many jumps you can do in 30 seconds).
    • One-foot jumping (alternate legs).
    • Side-to-side jumps.
    • Double jumps (jumping higher each time).

Benefits: Builds endurance, coordination, and cardiovascular fitness.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video demonstrating the challenges. The more you do, the more points you get in Flight Club!

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Take your pulse before and after this challenge. What was the difference? Use that evidence: was this an aerobic or anaerobic workout — or both?
  • Which challenge made you breathe the hardest? Why do you think that one pushed your cardiovascular system the most?

assignments.title: Week 12: Flight Club
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.6 · Nutrition
Week 12
🚀 Flight Club Challenge

After learning about nutrition, fuel up and try these three moves. Flamingo Balance trains stability, Butterfly opens your hips, and Arm Circles wake up your shoulders.

1
Flamingo Balance
  1. Stand up tall with your feet together.
  2. Gently lift one foot and bend your knee so your foot is behind you.
  3. Hold your arms out to the side like wings for balance.
  4. Try to stay still like a flamingo for 10 seconds.
  5. Switch legs and repeat.

Optional: Try closing one eye or flapping your "wings" for a fun challenge!

Benefits: Builds focus and body control, helping you stay calm and centered.

2
Butterfly Stretch

How to Do It:

  • Sit on the floor with feet together and knees bent outward.
  • Hold your feet with your hands and gently push your knees toward the floor.
  • Keep your back straight and hold the stretch.
  • Optional: Pretend your legs are butterfly wings and gently flap them!

Benefits: Stretches the inner thighs and hips.

3
Arm Circles
  1. Stand up straight with your arms stretched out to the sides, like a big "T."
  2. Slowly make small forward circles with your arms for 10 seconds.
  3. Then, switch directions and make small backward circles for 10 seconds.
  4. Want a challenge? Try making the circles bigger each time!

Optional: Pretend you're flying like a superhero or spinning like a windmill!

Benefits: Warms up your shoulder and arm muscles to get ready for movement.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video demonstrating the challenges. The more you do, the more points you get in Flight Club!

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which sense (vision, inner ear, proprioception) helped you balance during Flamingo? How do you know — try closing your eyes and see what changes.
  • Connect nutrition to this workout. What food would you want to eat AFTER this challenge to help your body recover? Why that specific food?

assignments.html:
Optima

5th Grade PE · Unit 1.7 · Locomotor Skills
Week 13

Design a VR locomotor course that asks a player to use 5+ different movement patterns. Coaches build these for real athletes too — combining patterns trains the brain to transition smoothly.

1
Step 1
Pick Your Environment

Choose an open space — beach, playground, trail, school gym, or forest.

2
Step 2
Build the Course

Use IFX tools and animations to create a course with at least 5 different locomotor skills. Arrange them in a path so the player flows from one skill to the next.

3
Step 3
Locomotor Skills to Include
  • Walking — steady, rhythmic steps
  • Running — faster, with arms pumping
  • Hopping — one foot only
  • Skipping — step-hop, step-hop
  • Jumping — both feet leaving the ground
  • Leaping — push off one foot, land on the other
  • Sliding — sideways movement
4
Step 4
Label by Color

Place signs, arrows, or IFX guides at each station. Use these colors:

  • Green – Walking
  • Blue – Running
  • Red – Jumping
  • Purple – Skipping
  • Yellow – Hopping

Optional: Add obstacles like bridges, cones, or tunnels for creative movement.

5
Step 5
Submit

Take a screenshot of your full course and upload!

📝Weekly Reflection

Which two locomotor skills are hardest to transition between? Why? Use what you know about coordination and motor patterns to explain.

assignments.title: Week 14: Flight Club
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.7 · Locomotor Skills
Week 14
🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Three strength moves that hit your legs, core, and arms. Locomotor skills depend on these muscle groups — this challenge builds the engine.

1
Split Squat
  1. Stand up tall with one foot in front and the other foot behind you — like you're about to take a big step.
  2. Keep your front knee over your ankle and your back heel lifted off the ground.
  3. Slowly bend both knees to lower your body straight down.
  4. Stop when your back knee is close to the ground (but not touching!).
  5. Stand back up. Do 5 slow squats, then switch legs and repeat.

Benefits: Makes your leg muscles stronger, especially your thighs and calves.

2
Superman Hold
  1. Lie flat on your stomach on the floor or a soft mat.
  2. Stretch your arms straight out in front of you and your legs straight behind you.
  3. At the same time, lift your arms, chest, and legs slightly off the ground.
  4. Try to hold this pose for 10 seconds — like you're flying through the sky!
  5. Slowly lower back down and rest. Try it again 2–3 more times!

Benefits: Strengthens your back and core muscles.

3
Bench Dips
  1. Find a sturdy chair, bench, or low table. Sit on the edge with your hands next to your hips.
  2. Walk your feet forward and slide your bottom off the edge, so your hands are holding you up.
  3. Bend your elbows to lower your body a little — like you're going down slowly.
  4. Push back up until your arms are straight again.
  5. Try doing 5–10 dips, then take a break!

Benefits: Strengthens your arms, shoulders, and chest.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video demonstrating the challenges. The more you do, the more points you get in Flight Club!

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which muscle group felt most worked after this challenge — quads, glutes, core, or arms? How do you know?
  • Which locomotor skill would benefit most from training these muscles? Pick one (running, jumping, leaping, skipping) and explain the connection.

assignments.title: Week 16: Flight Club
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.8 · Throwing & Catching
Week 16
🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Mix of flexibility and core work. These three target the muscle groups you need for throwing, catching, and staying balanced when an opponent crashes into your space.

1
Butterfly Stretch

How to Do It:

  • Sit on the floor with feet together and knees bent outward.
  • Hold your feet with your hands and gently push your knees toward the floor.
  • Keep your back straight and hold the stretch.
  • Optional: Pretend your legs are butterfly wings and gently flap them!

Benefits: Stretches the inner thighs and hips.

2
Forearm Plank

How to Do It:

  • Get into a plank position with arms straight and back flat.
  • Hold for 30 seconds without dropping your belly.
  • Challenge: Try tapping one shoulder at a time while holding the plank.

Modification: Try a knee plank if needed.

Benefits: Builds core and upper body strength.

3
Seated Forward Stretch

How to Do It:

  • Sit on the floor with legs straight in front of you.
  • Reach forward toward your toes while keeping your legs straight.
  • Hold the stretch for 10 seconds, then sit up slowly.

Benefits: Stretches hamstrings and lower back.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video demonstrating the challenges. The more you do, the more points you get in Flight Club!

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Why is core strength important for throwing and catching? Use what you know about the kinetic chain to explain.
  • Which felt harder — holding the plank or holding a stretch? Why? (Hint: think about muscular endurance vs. flexibility.)

quizzes.title: Quiz 1: Why We Move + Warm-Ups & Cool-Downs

questions.text: Marcus is about to play a soccer game. He has 10 minutes before kickoff. Which is the BEST way to spend that time?

answers.text: Sit on the bench so his muscles stay rested.
Do 5 minutes of light jogging followed by 5 minutes of dynamic stretches like leg swings and arm circles.
Do 10 minutes of long static stretches (holding each one for 60 seconds).
Eat a large meal to give him energy for the game.

questions.text: Why does a warm-up improve athletic performance — not just reduce injury?

answers.text: It tricks the brain into thinking you're already exercising.
It cools down your muscles so they save energy.
It raises core body temperature and lubricates joints, so muscles produce force faster.
It burns enough calories to give you extra energy for the workout.

questions.text: Which body system delivers oxygen to working muscles during exercise?

answers.text: The skeletal system (bones).
The cardiovascular system (heart, blood, and blood vessels).
The nervous system (brain and nerves).
The digestive system (stomach and intestines).

questions.text: Dynamic stretching (moving stretches) before activity can improve performance, while long static stretches before sprinting may actually reduce power.

answers.text: True
False

questions.text: What is the name for brain chemicals released during exercise that boost mood and reduce stress? (Starts with E.)

answers.text: endorphins
endorphin

quizzes.description: Five questions covering Modules 1.1–1.2. Test your understanding of physical activity benefits, the cardiovascular and muscular systems, and how to prep your body for movement.

quizzes.title: Quiz 2: Strength, Endurance & Cardio

questions.text: What is the difference between muscular strength and muscular endurance?

answers.text: Strength is for boys; endurance is for girls.
Strength is how much force a muscle can produce in one effort; endurance is how long a muscle can keep producing force.
Strength only uses your arms; endurance only uses your legs.
Strength is built with cardio; endurance is built with stretching.

questions.text: Jada is sprinting at full speed for 20 seconds during a relay race. Which fuel system is her body using the MOST?

answers.text: Aerobic — long, steady oxygen use.
Anaerobic — short bursts without oxygen as the main fuel.
Digestive — breaking down breakfast.
Skeletal — moving her bones with no muscles involved.

questions.text: Which muscle group is the strongest and most powerful in the body for running and jumping?

answers.text: Biceps (front of upper arm).
Triceps (back of upper arm).
Gluteus maximus (the glutes).
Masseter (jaw muscle).

questions.text: A trained endurance athlete can have a resting heart rate as low as 40 BPM because each beat pumps so much blood that the heart doesn't need to fire as often.

answers.text: True
False

questions.text: What's the term for your body's maximum rate of oxygen use during all-out exercise? (Two characters: a letter, a symbol, and a word.)

answers.text: VO2 max
VO₂ max
vo2 max
vo2max

quizzes.description: Five questions covering Modules 1.3–1.4. Test your understanding of muscular strength, muscular endurance, aerobic vs. anaerobic activity, and heart rate.

quizzes.title: Quiz 3: Flexibility & Nutrition

questions.text: What is the difference between active flexibility and passive flexibility?

answers.text: Active uses only your own muscles; passive uses outside help (gravity, a partner, or your hands).
Active happens during sports; passive happens when you sleep.
Active is hot stretching; passive is cold stretching.
They are exactly the same thing.

questions.text: Which of these is the BEST snack to eat 30 minutes before a long bike ride for steady energy?

answers.text: A bowl of plain ice cream (mostly sugar and fat).
A piece of whole-grain toast with peanut butter and banana (carbs + protein + healthy fat).
A can of soda only (just sugar, no protein or healthy carbs).
Nothing — your body works better empty.

questions.text: Riley wants to be able to touch their toes by the end of the month. Which plan will MOST LIKELY work?

answers.text: Touch their toes once, really hard, today only.
Hold a static toe-touch stretch for 20 seconds, 3–5 times a week, for 4 weeks.
Eat lots of bananas every day.
Bounce up and down while reaching for their toes for 60 seconds straight.

questions.text: Your body uses carbohydrates as its preferred fuel for movement, and stores extras in your muscles and liver as glycogen.

answers.text: True
False

questions.text: What is the U.S. Department of Agriculture's tool for healthy eating that splits a plate into fruits, vegetables, grains, protein, and dairy? (Two words run together, or hyphenated.)

answers.text: myplate
my plate
my-plate
